title: Ethiopia nutrition Make rule still invokes the legacy country food_acquired compiler as a prerequisite
body: Found during #1062's read-only sibling-write census. Ethiopia/_/Makefile:187-188 lists var/food_acquired.parquet as a prerequisite of the shared fct/nutrition target and runs nutrition.py. The declared nutrition builder itself obtains quantities from Country('Ethiopia').food_quantities(), so the legacy prerequisite can independently run Ethiopia/_/food_acquired.py, whose line 69 writes var/food_acquired.parquet without a framework cache hash. The rule also names fct, but fct is not declared by Ethiopia/_/data_scheme.yml and the current nutrition script writes only nutrition. No live Ethiopia build was run here. Diagnose a private cold/default/make sequence, compare raw/served food frames exactly, and inventory sibling hash/coverage before proposing retirement under #788. Coordinate with #771's separate FCT/API dependency; do not invoke the live FDC API or change scientific inputs by accident. Fix only after demonstrating the actual current route and exact values; old static 13-rules/12-country counts are stale after retirements.

title: Census residual: stale derived-food Make rules and Guatemala nutrition prerequisite still bypass framework authority
body: Current source census after Uganda #1062 finds var-consuming rules in Afghanistan/_/Makefile:14, CotedIvoire/_/Makefile:17, Togo/_/Makefile:14 and Guatemala/_/Makefile:31, besides Ethiopia. The first three still name removed food_acquired.py and food_prices_quantities_and_expenditures.py scripts; they are stale legacy rules, not demonstrated current API corruption. Guatemala nutrition directly consumes legacy food_quantities/fct and has raw food/FCT Make prerequisites. Diagnose actual normal and explicit-Make routes in private caches before deciding whether to retire dead rules or route required inputs through the framework. No builds/acquisition or code edits were performed outside Uganda. These countries are outside the eight-country LSMS-ISA campaign.
